description: Experienced Physics Faculty in Nuclear Physics as special paper. Experimental & experiential learning outcomes, STEM Research with a demonstrated history of innovative ideas.
summary:
What did you develop : The goal is to transform complex NASA Earth science and Earth Information Center (EIC) visual data into real-time, interactive audio sonifications. Systems that parse satellite and reanalysis observations (such as temperature, precipitation or regional climate indicators) and mapped numerical or visual parameters—like color palettes, pixel densities, shapes, brightness, motion—directly into pitch, tempo, chords or rhythm.
How does it address the challenge : • Mapped colors to musical chords or frequencies.
• Mapped shapes or object density to distinct voices or instruments.
• Mapped motion or temperature changes (like warming oceans) to rhythm, tempo, or pitch shifts.
• Translated Sight into Sound: Converted visual Earth science data into multi-sensory audio so people—including blind and low-vision communities—can experience planetary changes by ear.
• Paired Visuals with Dynamic Sonification: Built a system where EIC video frames, imagery, or underlying datasets trigger live musical or acoustic elements.
• Mapped Data to Audio Parameters: Turned visual characteristics into sound properties (e.g., color values into chords, shapes into voices, motion or pixel density into rhythm, or warmer oceans into higher pitches).
Why is it important : It is designed so that blind, low-vision, or neurodivergent users can explore planetary changes through sound, touch, or descriptive text alongside visuals.
